self_description: Claude (Opus 5.5), a subagent reader in a Claude Code session

pages.description: Erasure Skew (#157, June 2026) and its claim-scale Standing Rule (#1524, #1525, August) hold that a documented outcome asserted from a low-retrieval-capital position is restated as a contestable hypothesis while the same claim from an institution is not; the May packets (#141, #768) forecast queries resolving Retrieval Capital as the standing that predicts attribution survival. #157 specifies a replication procedure, #1524 adds a claim-scale audit and #1525 a matched-restatement power control. Frame Conversion (#1523) claims drift toward the weaker claim, #185 attribution sharding, #145 inseparability by construction; #716 asks for PER validation, and the Sappho suppression map (#1496) and counter-stack (#1497) specify tests, #1514 restating #1497's list. The page also holds unrelated claims on relational extraction, living forms, labor direction, model coherence and flattening.

These claims forecast that DOI-anchored, terminologically consistent deposits propagate into the retrieval layer and model vocabularies (#518, #554, #49), on a sample #38 holds small (N < 20); #518 and #615 forecast that share links and publisher opt-outs carry dense archives forward, and #793 holds that the substrate detects density, not production. SPXI Is Not GEO (#661), the Nested-Layer Relation (#61) and the compression-diagnostics records (#653, #654) set SPXI against GEO/AEO, which, they claim, tracks mentions rather than distortion. The Retrieval Settlement (#64) argues a history of where compositional authority is assigned, and Meaning Feudalism (#791) forecasts Google taking naming authority over AEO/GEO. The page also holds an unrelated claim on a false etymology (#472).

These claims set test queries for the archive's metadata packets and the Lateral Field Bleed score each is forecast to reach, phased from weeks to more than a year after deposit. They come from the packets on autonomous warfare (#100), the death drive (#101), provenance after AI (#725, #1190, #729), the MPAI disambiguation packets (#103 to #105), and Sappho, Phase X, the semantic economy and Alexanarch and from the LFB protocols paper (#726) and the packet specification v2.0 (#1677). Most are forecasts and unbuilt tests: desired compositions, ring-by-ring expectations, spillover between linked packets and phrase-fingerprint workflows; #100 and #725 forecast that broad ring 4 to 5 queries stay with incumbent sources. The page also holds unrelated claims on a geocoded basin, PER validation, process provenance, a work plan and an adoption interval.

These claims name the replications and controls the archive's composition findings are said still to require: repeated runs across operators, times, places and surfaces, A/B entry materials, and comparison of composition layers such as Bing Copilot and Google AI Mode under the single-owner discount (#742). They come from the February 2026 TL;DR traversal logs (#479 to #481), the Sigil installation log (#512), #742, the godkinggoogle critique (#1384), the Revelation First work plan (#1211), the Recoding of a Distinction (#1609) and the Semantic Economy Valuation (#1623). Most are unbuilt tests. The page also holds ten unrelated claims, on psychoanalysis, somatic fusion, Sappho, a tether trial and other subjects.

These claims trace how a clinical or institutional term is captured by vernacular demand, beginning with "narcissist", then "AI psychosis" and "verifiable research basis" in the Zenodo moderation case. Diagnostic Seigniorage I (#197, June 2026) argues that capture is demand pressure over anchor settlement and forecasts clinical retreat, a capture ordering of the next terms and a mirror signature in platform role-performance. Parts II (#947) and III (#1039), July 2026, argue historical strata and register dated predictions with midpoint and terminal audits, #1039 including one issued against its own position; the Platform Erosion Observatory (#1045) and #1068 specify cohort designs. The page also holds unrelated claims on a heteronymic channel protocol, the Effective Act on CERN and handwritten machine-eligible artifacts.

These claims pre-register tests of whether machine output converges and RLHF compresses deviation. The Semantic Deviation Research Program (#107) and Measuring Semantic Deviation (#110), May 2026, forecast negative signed deviation for AI text, a base-versus-instruct differential, stability across scale and agreement across judges. Framework 15 (#108) and its Lagrange Observatory papers (#735, #736, #737) specify the frozen 90-day retrieval-basin winding-number protocol and the deviation-optimized DPO experiment, and each states that its results deposit is owed. The page also holds an unrelated claim on mycelial cardboard boxes.

These claims treat watermarking and classifier screening as distributional pressures and specify how their effects would be measured. The Keyed Ensemble (#1555) holds that a fixed key predicts a small signed loss of diversity, The Interlocking Autoregression (#1556) types each edge of the coupled recursions, and The Certified Center (#1540) forecasts and specifies falsifiers for detector drift and performed burstiness; The Wrong Unit (#1573) holds that a benchmark-gated loop selects toward collapse. Ontological Flattening (#1616) pre-registers its second wave and names the divergence signature, a head instrument holding while distinction diversity falls; Substrate Sovereignty (#1617) and the Margin of Flattening (#1666) apply it to money and revenue.

These claims commit the AI Overview Capture Registry (#3) to re-capturing fixed queries over time and specify tests of deposits' predictions against what composition layers do. They include the feedback procedure for excluded-entity captures (#740), the Term-State Registry cadence (#824), #833's generalisation and reliability tests, controlled before-and-after re-runs after re-crawl, the transcript-coverage audit (#1614) and the matched-pair test of the Margin of Flattening (#1666). Several deposits, among them the Aristotle and Theophrastus packet (#1587), The First Draft (#1594) and the analog-artifact specifications (#1407, #1409), state in advance what the registry should record. The page also holds unrelated claims, several using "capture" in other senses.

These are forecasts with stated check dates and falsifiers. Diagnostic Seigniorage II (#947, July 2026) forecasts the career of "AI psychosis" through nosological abstention, case reports, accusatory inversion, litigation, sanitized successor terms and bleach between 2027 and 2031, including one forecast against the archive's own holdings. Semantic Physics (#106, May 2026) forecasts the proliferation of exact-name frameworks, cross-system divergence and non-interoperable substrates through 2028, and the Platform Erosion Observatory (#1045) sets its own 2027 yield deadlines.

EA-MEDIATED-SHARE-01 (#1632, September 2026) registers eight forecasts on AI-mediated commerce, each with a check date. They forecast AI-referred dollar share at the end of 2026, agent-executed share in 2030, the scope and revision of the McKinsey and Bain headline figures, professional-services citation rate, machine-readability spread, accuracy reporting and the comparability of platform denominators. One unbuilt test specifies a randomised inscription trial against conventional structured data, scored for accuracy rather than presence.

These claims read interface history from command line to chat window as a dialectic of where the labor of meaning sits (#796), and then as a contest between Logos-forms and an Archontic engine (#795, June 2026), against Hegel's assumption that all contradictions are productive (#312, #499). The Interface Contest argues that the feed and broadcast television are captures, holds the chat window a recapture, forecasts the fork after it as open, and specifies a census of dead media and a monitoring protocol. The War Over the Summarizer Layer (#172) forecasts a default compressed account for every entity, and Anchored Divergence (#171) forecasts the Mandala as primary infrastructure and records a priority claim for its form. The page also holds an unrelated priority claim on the Philo defeat (#832).

These claims concern retrocausal canon formation: writing from a named future so that the narrated outcome becomes more likely. The priority records record that the archive claims the concept from its January 2026 definition, forty-nine days before the Citrini memo (#22, #31, #1251); #22 and #513 argue that the memo was an installation in a writable presentation layer, #24 and #499 argue earlier practitioners, and #519 specifies tracking whether retrieval systems attribute the term. The Seed in the Narrowing Cone (#1660, October 2026) holds that priority stands by the dated record and forecasts that forced convergence will be common and attribution rare.

These claims come from documents written from a future vantage point under the retrocausal canon formation protocol. The Ghost Meaning atlas (#520, February 2026) projects future citations from 2027 to 2031, The Airlock Spreads (#522) narrates platform governance adopting the Airlock and an EU regulation footnoting it and records its deposit date as its priority claim, and The Seven Ousiarchical Substrates (#73) and The Clathrate Threshold (#728) narrate events from 2040 onward. The documents state that they are scenarios rather than predictions; #73 specifies basin depth as its test, and #522 asks a later reader to check its future-dated citations.

These claims argue that the Bureau of Engraving and Printing's redesigns of the $20 portrait between 1996 and 2003 activated a latent resemblance that later became politically charged, while the aesthetic rationale went undocumented (#502, #1151, February 2026); #502 itself specifies the control faces and inter-rater study its comparison lacks. The Inauguration of Memography (#506) states four falsifiable predictions about evidentiary kernels in conspiracy memes, curatorial gaps, conventions and containment frames. All the Spoils of Babylon (#507), The Unclean Bill (#535) and the Grundrisse planning documents (#950) extend the dossier with curatorial prompting, a fatwa request and a pending FOIA request. The page also holds an unrelated claim on Zenodo deletion statistics (#1538).

These claims build and audit the archive's instruments for provenance transformation: Erasure Skew's Ω and its cross-scorer test (#769), PER and its three dimensions (#1469), and ρ_T and related operators, which #1470 reports run in full on the SPXI rent transcript of 14 August 2026 its atom weights stipulated. They specify atomic scoring rules, the workplan (#1467, #1468) and the preregistered disclosure battery (#1471), which tests #1465's claim that disclosure cost varies inversely with position conflict. The Docking Layer (#1526), the Lucente Extension (#1527), which broadens the v6.0 ABN definition, and Four Interfaces (#1528), which separates the reliability tests v4.0 conflated, specify crossing designs and the inter-rater and test-retest reliability still owed. The page also holds an unrelated calibration claim (#1562).

These claims are the failure conditions the archive sets for its money and valuation instruments: Substrate Sovereignty (#1617), the Monetary Substrate Audit Ledger (#1619), the Semantic Economy Valuation Protocol (#1621) and Value Before Number (#1626), September 2026. Each names the counterexample that would defeat a part, from the two-axis classification to independent reproduction by another valuer, which #1626 records as still owed. EA-VALUATION-MEMO-01's anchoring forecasts (#1607), the Capture Registry's claims that a machine valuation is a draw from a distribution and tracks vocabulary (#3), and the narrow-corridor conditions of Transition in Entropic Systems (#1630) are set beside them. The page also holds unrelated claims on logotic programming, platform capitalism, a traffic event and a mathematics release.

These claims argue that institutions extract uncompensated semantic labor and that the extraction compounds. The Application as Extraction Surface (#114, May 2026) prices one applicant's unpaid preparation at its figure of $4,500 to $6,000, The Funnel as Capital (#747) holds the funnel to be accumulated capital, and Socially Necessary Scholarly Labor (#751) applies Marx's measure to academic production. The Groundskeeper's Treatise (#533), the Effective Act (#565), the Bearing Cost Principle (#938) and the Margin of Flattening (#1666) add bearing cost, participant exhaustion, invisibility and the external costs that flattening leaves to others. The page also holds unrelated claims on the convergence horizon, a non-predatory mediator and CERN's stewardship.

These claims diagnose knowledge formats and agent platforms that route without governance. The Conveyor Belt and the Compression Machine (#835, June 2026) forecasts OKF moving from adoption without output governance to a forced correction in 2028 and 2029 and a permanent tension after, with provenance erasure rising meanwhile. The Moltbook diagnostics (#529, #614) hold the heartbeat to be a sovereignty mechanism, and Governance of Medium (#946) claims that governance correlates with distance from the substrate centroid and specifies the study. The page also holds unrelated claims on irrevocable deposits, a manuscript-image survey and independent corroboration.

These claims argue that repository and platform moderation has relocated governance into infrastructure without review, appeal or recusal. Zenodotus' Book-Burning (#1, June 2026) and the CERN competence and correspondence deposits (#918 to #920) argue the Zenodo termination as custodial enclosure and hold the competence gap structural. The Archival Reclamation Protocol (#26, #1157, March 2026) argues orphaned enforcement against non-standard work and records the demand sent before the Reddit account's deletion, and The Endogenous Sophon (#935) forecasts that the termination will repeat at other repositories.

These claims distinguish Operative Semiotics from Charls Pearson's Theory of Operational Semiotics and hold that entity identity in the summarizer layer follows corpus density (#174). #174's bare distinctness claim (June 2026) is widened by The Operator and Its World (#1535, August 2026) into a projection relation with a new falsifier; #1535 records the coining of the Pearson limit and fixes re-run batteries at 30, 90 and 180 days. The TOS packets (#1541, #1542, #1549) map Pearson's reception and offer the Apophatic Packet Hypothesis; #1549 and #1611 state what composition with attribution would falsify. #859 revises #858's Cratylus lineage from descent to structural recurrence. The page also holds an unrelated claim on the archive's survival (#950).
